items.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024
items.q: And I saw a show the other day and I think it was Quincy Jones said — and he was talking about Miles Davis.

ctx.x: Yes I know there was some kind of historical reference there. Would there be any pop music of the day in your record collection? Let’s say early rock & roll or, you know, later on Motown etcetera?

No. I just had a period where I was in the studios playing that kind of music but the jazz musicians always — and it was reciprocated, that is jazz musicians always knew that we were far above the rock & roll players. And rock & roll players always admired us as real musicians. But that’s no longer the case. And I saw a show the other day and I think it was Quincy Jones said — and he was talking about Miles Davis. He said, “When money comes in the room God leaves.” I wouldn’t go that far but it’s certainly…
Yes. I remember reading a quote from you that — I believe you stated jazz is still an art form because money can’t really be a part of it — or something like that.
